walkthroughs.body_html:
Literary Texts and Films — a core area of A-Level Spanish.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Literary Texts and Films brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Literary Texts and Films.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct reflexive: '___ casé en 2020'?
options: me
se
te
nos

mcqs.q: When was same-sex marriage legalised in Spain?
Where do object pronouns go in 'I see him' (lo veo)?
options: Either position is correct.
It is a typo for 'Yo gusto'.
Before the conjugated verb: 'Lo veo'.
After the verb: 'Veo lo'.

mcqs.q: Which preposition expresses purpose ('in order to')?
options: Por.
Either, interchangeably.
Para - 'Estudio PARA aprender'.
Either position is correct.

mcqs.q: Why does 'Me gusta el chocolate' literally translate as 'Chocolate is pleasing to me'?
options: Gustar means 'to like' and works exactly like English.
Either position is correct.
Gustar works backwards - the thing liked is the subject, the person is the indirect object.
It is a typo for 'Yo gusto'.
